name: Files
tagline: FTP, FTPS and SFTP servers where partners drop files and your app picks them up.
point: ftp://localhost:2121 (passive mode; FTPS with the Test CA)
user or user@server; a user with no password takes any password except wrong

capabilities.title: Three protocols, one folder
capabilities.text: Each server is a folder: FTP, explicit FTPS and SFTP all see the same files, so the app can switch protocol without new fixtures.

capabilities.title: The commands EDI clients use
capabilities.text: PASV, EPSV, LIST, NLST, MLSD, RETR, STOR, APPE, DELE, MKD, RMD, RNFR/RNTO, SIZE, MDTM and REST.

capabilities.title: Drop a partner's file
capabilities.text: put_file puts text or binary on a server; the app finds it on its next poll, exactly as if the partner sent it.

capabilities.title: Wait for the app's upload
capabilities.text: wait_for_file blocks until a file whose path matches a * pattern appears, then returns it.

capabilities.title: Users and read-only logins
capabilities.text: Each server has its own users; read_only users get permission denied on writes, as a real partner account would.

capabilities.title: Every login and transfer
capabilities.text: list_transfers shows logins, uploads, downloads, deletes and listings, newest first, with the provoked ones marked.

capabilities.title: A stable host key
capabilities.text: The SFTP host key is kept on disk, so a client that pinned it keeps trusting it across restarts.

capabilities.title: Failures on the next session
capabilities.text: Refuse logins, fill the disk, deny permission, cut a transfer after 4 KB, slow to 20 KB/s or change the host key.

excerpts.title: A server, its folders and the next sessions

callouts.title: How to connect
callouts.text: SFTP on :2222, FTP on :2121 and FTPS with AUTH TLS, all on the same server.

callouts.title: Folders
callouts.text: Folders made by set_file_server, such as /in for the app and /out for the partner.

callouts.title: What the app uploaded
callouts.text: A file's content as text; get_file returns base64 for binary.

callouts.title: Put a file
callouts.text: Drop a file as if the partner did; the app picks it up on its next poll.

callouts.title: Provoke
callouts.text: Login refused (530), disk full (552), permission denied (550), drop after 4 KB, slow, host key changed.

callouts.title: Users and folders
callouts.text: Each user with its folders: files waiting in /in, files the app wrote to /out.

callouts.title: An upload
callouts.text: Who uploaded, which path, size and how long it took.

callouts.title: Refused login
callouts.text: A provoked login_refused is marked on the row, so it is not taken for a real bug.

callouts.title: Did the app retry?
callouts.text: A provoked disk full is marked on the row, next to what the app did after it.

callouts.title: The file itself
callouts.text: Fixed-width EDI shown as text; the exact bytes are kept.

provoke.name: Host key changed
provoke.what: SFTP shows another host key; pinned clients refuse

provoke.name: Read-only partner
provoke.what: A user that can read but gets permission denied on writes

provoke.name: Wrong password
provoke.what: Users with no password take any password except wrong

advantages.title: No partner to call
advantages.text: Real partner servers are shared, slow to change and never fail on request. Here you make the file appear, or the disk fill, now.

advantages.title: Proof of what was sent
advantages.text: Every upload is kept and listed, so a test asserts the exact file the app wrote, not just that it connected.

advantages.title: Three protocols for free
advantages.text: FTP, FTPS and SFTP from one process and one folder, with no SSH daemon or vsftpd to configure.

advantages.title: Failures that end
advantages.text: A provocation lasts until you set none, and every provoked session is marked in the transfer list.

agent.prompt: Drop an orders file on the EDI server, then check that the app answers with a file in /out.
